topic: OpenAI halved what the $200 Pro plan buys; Aaron priced his own 30-day AI coding bill at API list
thesis: A subscription with a published exchange rate is a bill you can read: every OpenAI tier now costs $20 per 1x Plus, and in one heavy user's agentic-coding bill the dominant line item is cache reads (the re-read), so the cache-read price and the choice of model matter more than the vendor.

sources.notes: Aaron's own copy of the subscriber email (Chinese localization). Used for plan terms only; never shown on screen (private account context).
Secondary report of the Pro 200 change and the new Pro 500 tier (25x Plus, Ultrafast).

sources.notes: Full sentence: 'if you do the math, it will net out at half the dollar in API spend compared to the old Pro $200 plan.' Text read from search-result rendering; the on-screen excerpt is an exact substring shown with ellipses.
Live API price sheet retrieved 2026-09-30 (GPT-6 Astra $10/$1.00/$50; GPT-6.1 Sol $2/$0.10/$10 per 1M).
Live API price sheet retrieved 2026-09-30 (Opus 5 $5/$0.50/$25; Opus 5.5 $4/$0.20/$20; Fable 5.1 $10/$0.25/$50 per 1M).
Thread on the Pro $200 re-opening (74 points / 90 comments at retrieval). Quote shown exactly and attributed to 'Hacker News commenter'.
Source of the ~10 hours before the DevDay keynote timing (his account).

sources.publisher: Aaron Guo (own session logs priced at API list)
sources.notes: One Mac, 2026-08-31..09-29. API list price, not what Aaron paid. On-screen Codex figures are the Pro account only (≈$3,600; Astra $2,884, 78% cache reads); the second account is excluded for privacy.
Author's own plans, decisions and labeled forecasts.

facts.claim: From 2026-10-30 Pro 200 Codex and ChatGPT Work usage drops from 20x to 10x the Plus allowance at the same $200 price; existing subscribers keep current limits through 2026-10-29.
Existing Pro 200 subscribers receive one-time credits worth $2,500 that expire 2026-12-31.
Tibo, who leads Codex, wrote that the new plan 'will net out at half the dollar in API spend' compared with the old Pro $200 plan.
After Oct 30 every tier prices usage at $20 per 1x Plus (Plus $20/1x, Pro 100 $100/5x, Pro 200 $200/10x, Pro 500 $500/25x); the old Pro 200 ($200/20x = $10 per 1x) was the only bulk discount.
Pro 500 costs $500 for 25x Plus and is the only tier with Ultrafast speed in Codex.
The cut was announced about ten hours before OpenAI's DevDay keynote (as reported on X).
A Hacker News commenter wrote: "Simply say 'we're cutting limits in half.' Five words." Several commenters said they had moved to Claude Opus 5.5.
One X user estimated the old plan at about $14k a month in API value, the new one about $7k, and Claude Max about $8k; methodology not shown and unverified.
Aaron pays $200 a month for ChatGPT Pro and $200 for Claude Max and priced 30 days of session logs from his main machine at API list price.
At API list price over 30 days on one machine: Claude Code about $9,400; Codex on the Pro account about $3,600 (a floor). Not what Aaron paid.
The Pro account's Codex weekly meter reached 99-100% in five of six September windows.
Cache reads were 78% of GPT-6 Astra cost (Pro account), 76% of Claude Opus 5 and 58% of Claude Opus 5.5 at list price.
Aaron's Claude Code sessions read about 17 billion tokens from cache in 30 days (17.44B across models, one machine).

List prices per 1M tokens (input / cache read / output): GPT-6 Astra $10 / $1.00 / $50; Claude Opus 5 $5 / $0.50 / $25; Claude Fable 5.1 $10 / $0.25 / $50; Claude Opus 5.5 $4 / $0.20 / $20; GPT-6.1 Sol $2 / $0.10 / $10.
The same Astra tokens priced at GPT-6.1 Sol fall from $2,884 to $353 (about 12%); Opus 5 tokens priced at Opus 5.5 fall from $6,559 to $3,250 (about half). Price only; quality not compared.
Worked example: Opus 5 cache reads of 9.96B tokens x $0.50 per 1M is about $4,980 at list (76% of the $6,559 Opus 5 line).
On 2026-09-06 Aaron published 'I Put GPT-6 Astra to Work', praising Astra for carrying a whole deployment without handing it back.
Aaron's decisions: Claude Max stays his main tool; keep Pro 200 through Dec 31 to use the credits and not buy Pro 500; run Codex on GPT-6.1 Sol for a week in October.
Aaron's labeled inferences: the 20x language fades into visible dollar budgets; competition moves to cache-read and speed pricing; heavy-user subsidies keep shrinking.
